doc.title: Ashley Keating and Allan Whitworth Interview, 1963-03-22

title: Dixieland Hall, the Paddock and tourist-oriented music
summary: Keating says the bands at Dixieland Hall played crowd-pleasing commercial music, and he could not afford the Paddock.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: very young. They never did give me his name. He didn't play. He, he was there. That's, that's strange the way it, it goes. Uh, what about the bands at Preservation Hall and Dixieland Hall and the Paddock or anything like that? Have you heard those?

Uh, we've heard a couple at, uh, Dixieland Hall. Uh, unfortunately there seemed to be some pressure on them to play, uh, a tourist type of music. We didn't stay along in either case. Uh, one band was Paul Barberans, I think, and another one was led by Frog Jazz. Although the personnel of both bands seemed to be relatively similar. Uh, I don't think it had appealed.
All right. See, this is a reel two of Ashley Keating and Alan Whitworth. All right, we were talking about your impression of Dixieland Hall and Hall Barber and Kit Howard's band there.

That's right, yes. Well, those bands seem to be under pressure to play a crowd-pleasing commercial style, certainly not of a great deal of interest to the enthusiast of New Orleans music. The paddock, we never did get inside. Of course, we're doing this on a limited budget and 90 cents for a drink is a little more than we can afford, particularly as we don't drink unless it's to hear some famous musician.
